Penn State is 2-1 ATS and covering by 5.8 a game; Wisconsin is 1-2 and minus 0.7.

A 17.5-point spread also caps the second half. The favorite that is grinding by construction has less reason to keep throwing, and the underdog that cannot generate explosive plays has no fast way back.

totals.game: Northern Illinois Huskies @ Georgia State Panthers
facts: 0-3, 24 points scored in two graded games

paras: Book has 56.5, the model 51.3. Georgia State can get most of the way there on their own, so this is a bet about whether Northern Illinois contributes anything.

Northern Illinois is 0-3 and has been outscored by 23.0 a game. The offense ranks 128th in Success Rate, 137th in Finishing Drives and 115th in Explosiveness, on a 51.9 offense grade and a 45.5 run block grade, with 24 points scored across two graded games. Georgia State is the live half. They are 2-1, 3-0 ATS covering by 15.2 a game, with 90 points in two graded games and a 90.5 passing grade behind an 81.1 pass block grade. Their offense ranks 35th in Success Rate.

The exposure is Georgia State's finishing: their defense ranks 121st in Finishing Drives, so opponents who reach the red zone convert. Northern Illinois getting there is the whole question, and 137th in Finishing Drives is the answer the season has given so far. This is also the third straight week the board has pointed at a Georgia State game; the previous two were spreads fading them, and both lost.

Book has 58.5, the model 59.9, so raw this is a 1.4-point Over lean. With two defenses of this quality the slate fit expects the model to be 6.5 points over the book, which leaves a 5.1-point residual to the Under.

The scoring records are the Over case and they are built on schedule. Both teams are 3-0, Missouri by 22.3 a game and Mississippi State by 27.0, with 92 and 100 points in two graded games. What they have allowed is the more useful number: 17.5 and 13.0 a game.

Missouri's defense ranks 16th in Success Rate and 5th in Havoc with an 80.2 pass rush grade. Mississippi State's ranks 37th in Success Rate on an 87.2 run defense grade and an 82.3 coverage grade. A 58.5 total asks each of these offenses for 29 against the best defense either has seen.

Mississippi State's tempo is the reason this is the least comfortable of the five: 24.3 seconds a snap, 10th nationally, and their games have gone 11.2 points over the posted total. Missouri's own weak spot is Explosiveness allowed, 134th, so one long play changes the arithmetic here faster than in the other four.
Book has 44.5, the model 48.3. With two defenses ranked outside the top 95 the fit expects a slight Under lean, so the residual is +4.5.

What the two teams have allowed is the case: 27.5 a game for Rice and 21.0 for Fresno State, 48.5 combined against a total of 44.5. Rice's defense ranks 102nd in Success Rate and 116th in Finishing Drives; Fresno State's ranks 97th in Success Rate.

Neither offense is good enough to make this comfortable. Rice ranks 87th in Success Rate and 131st in Explosiveness with 31 points in two graded games; Fresno State ranks 129th in Success Rate and has a 36.8 pass block grade, though they rank 20th in Explosiveness, which is the one way this gets to 45 quickly.
This is the thinnest of the five and is sized the same as the rest only because the card is flat. A 13-point spread with two offenses this inefficient is the profile that produces a 24-17 game.

Baugh has 438 rushing yards in three games, 146.0 a game, against a line of 119.0. The projection is 149.8. He has 55 carries, 18.3 a game, and an 8.0 yards per carry average that is not going to hold; the line only asks for 6.5 on the same volume.

The efficiency is earned rather than lucky in the way that matters here. His run grade is 91.7 and his offense grade 90.1, with 27 avoided tackles, 255 yards after contact, 10 explosive runs and a long of 75. A 64.2% breakaway share does mean the yardage arrives unevenly, which is the risk on a line this high.

Ole Miss is the matchup. Their tackling grade is 42.5, the weakest unit on either roster in this game, against a back whose distinguishing 2026 number is 27 broken tackles. Their defense ranks 96th in Success Rate and 114th in Field Position, and the run defense grade of 68.6 is the only defensive number above 62.5 they carry.

Florida are 3.5-point home favorites with a 31.0 implied team total against a league average of 26.4, so the script supports carries rather than working against them. Baugh is not a receiving threat, 2 targets on 32 routes, so this is a pure ground projection.
Rule has 329 rushing yards in three games, 109.7 a game, against a line of 66.5. The projection is 106.9. The line asks for 5.25 yards a carry on his 12.7 carries a game; he is at 8.7.

The caveat is where those yards come from. His breakaway share is 55.9%, so more than half the production is long runs, and the volume is modest for a lead back. What supports it is the contact running underneath: 217 yards after contact on 38 carries, 9 avoided tackles, 10 explosive runs, an 84.2 run grade and an 86.0 offense grade with no fumbles.

Nebraska's offense ranks 5th in Explosiveness and 6th in Finishing Drives on a 90.7 run grade, and they have scored 105 points across two graded games. Michigan State's defense ranks 90th in Success Rate; their run defense grade of 77.1 is respectable but their 61.0 tackling grade is not.

This is the same game as the Nebraska -5.5 spread, so the two positions are correlated. Nebraska's implied total is 27.0 against a 26.4 league average, and at a 5.5-point spread there is no blowout script to take the ball out of his hands in the fourth quarter.
Smothers has 198 rushing yards in three games, 66.0 a game, against a line of 52.0. He has 41 carries at 4.8 a carry; the line asks for 3.8 on the same volume.

The model's 101.8 is not the number to bet into. It carries a 1.384 pace and script multiplier, the highest on any pick here, which is doing more work than the underlying rate does. The honest projection is his own production adjusted for the matchup, which lands in the 66 to 75 range, and that is still comfortably clear of 52.0.

He is a big-play back: 31.8% breakaway share, 5 explosive runs, a long of 45, 11 avoided tackles and 140 yards after contact on a 77.1 run grade. Tennessee's tackling grade is 56.4 against a 65.9 run defense grade, the softer half of a defense that is otherwise strong through the air at 89.4 coverage and 79.0 pass rush.

Texas is a 5.5-point road underdog with a 30.2 implied total, the highest of any team on this prop card. The risk is the split: he has 13.7 carries a game rather than a true workhorse share, so a negative script costs him more than it would a 20-carry back.

facts: 10.9% breakaway share, long run of 15 all season
paras: Howard has 138 rushing yards in three games, 46.0 a game, against a line of 59.5. The projection is 35.3. At his 12.3 carries a game the line asks for 4.8 yards a carry; he is at 3.7.

The reason this is an Under rather than a coin flip is the absence of a long run. His breakaway share is 10.9% and his longest carry of the season is 15 yards, across 37 attempts. A back at 3.7 a carry with no explosive plays has to be given volume he is not getting to reach 59.5; 13 first downs on 37 carries says he is being used to stay on schedule.

The underlying grades are ordinary rather than bad: 71.5 run grade, 68.5 offense, 8 avoided tackles and 122 yards after contact. He is not a receiving outlet either, 6 targets on 49 routes for 26 yards at a minus 1.7 average depth of target.

UCLA's defense ranks 52nd in Success Rate and tied 5th in Field Position on a 67.7 run defense grade. The game is close to a pick, Maryland +1.5 with a 27.5 implied total, so there is no script that forces extra carries on him either way.

facts: 12.8 average depth of target, 1.74 yards per route run
paras: Tibbs has 15 catches in three games, 5.0 a game, against a line of 3.5. The projection is 5.1. He has run 93 routes and drawn 22 targets, 7.3 a game, which is the volume that makes four catches a normal outcome rather than a good one.

He is the field-stretcher rather than the possession option: 12.8 average depth of target, 10.8 yards a reception, 1.74 yards per route run, 60% on contested catches and 2 drops. A 12.8 aDOT does add variance to a receptions line, since the completion rate on those throws is lower than on a checkdown.

Kansas State's implied team total is 31.0 against a 26.4 league average, the highest on this card, and they are 6.5-point road favorites with 105 points scored in two graded games. Their passing grade is only 58.5, which is the honest argument against a receiving prop here; what the offense does grade well is protection, 86.1 pass block, and that is what keeps a 7-target-a-game route runner on schedule.

Cincinnati's coverage grade is 90.0, the strongest defensive number on either side, and their defense ranks tied 28th in Havoc. That is the argument against, and it is why this is a receptions line rather than a yardage line: volume survives good coverage better than efficiency does.
